Randall Nickerson directed a film about a famous mass UFO sighting at a school in Zimbabwe, and he has spent years collecting abduction accounts. With Danny Jones, he argues that alien abduction activity is surging and that the reports have put military authorities on alert.

Nickerson works from witness interviews gathered over decades, and he treats consistent testimony as data the official world ignores at its peril. Jones presses him on the newest cases and the military angle. Skeptics explain abduction reports through sleep and psychology, and Nickerson knows and rejects those answers. The episode preserves a veteran investigator's current assessment of his field. Listeners can weigh a lifetime of interviews against the simpler explanations, and hear why the man who collected them finds those explanations empty.

AI safety scholar Roman Yampolskiy joins Danny Jones to give the worst case for smart machines. The episode title quotes the stark line: if they build it, everyone dies. Yampolskiy has warned for years that super smart AI cannot be held in check.

Yampolskiy explains why he thinks a machine far smarter than us would not stay in its box. He walks through the ways such a mind could end the human story. Jones asks if any guard could work. Listeners get the darkest view in the AI debate, from a top voice for that side. The library files it as an archive record.
